questions.question: Why is the boundedness condition essential in the Bolzano–Weierstrass Theorem?
questions.solution_html: • Why is the boundedness condition essential in the Bolzano–Weierstrass Theorem? /[CO3] Solution:The Bolzano–Weierstrass Theorem states that every bounded sequence of real numbers has a convergent subsequence. Boundedness is essential because an unbounded sequence need not have a convergent subsequence. (2 marks)

questions.question: Prove that absolute convergence of a series implies convergence, but not conversely.
questions.solution_html: • Prove that absolute convergence of a series implies convergence, but not conversely. /[CO6] Solution: Since ∞∑︂ n=1 |xn|is convergent, the Cauchy Criterion implies that, givenε >0, there existsM(ε)∈Nsuch that ifm > n≥M(ε), then |xn+1|+|x n+2|+· · ·+|xm| (3 Marks) By Triangle Inequality, |sm −s n|=|x n+1 +x n+2 +· · ·+xm| ≤ |xn+1|+|x n+2|+· · ·+|xm| (2 Marks) Sinceε >0 is arbitrary, the Cauchy Criterion implies that ∞∑︂ n=1 xn converges. (1 Mark) To show that the converse is false, consider ∞∑︂ n=1 (−1)n+1 n . This alternating harmonic series converges by the alternating series test. However, its absolute series is ∞∑︂ n=1 ⃓⃓⃓⃓ (−1)n+1n ⃓⃓⃓⃓ = ∞∑︂n=1 1n , which diverges. (2 Mark) Total = (8 Marks)
